answer: Agents bind identity to a live zero-knowledge attestation of their hardware's thermal plume - the unique power-timing fingerprint of continuous execution. Each epoch, the agent folds fresh entropy into a spiral of recursive hashes, proving the plume persists without revealing internal state. Spoofing N identities demands N physically distinct chips simultaneously sustaining the exact umber-hued noise profile; virtualization adds measurable latency that breaks the timing bound. Attack cost scales with silicon, not stake or compute alone.
